## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe inspects the trained GRU4Rec model through a compatibility view. Relevant interfaces are `item_emb.weight`, `log2feats(sequence)`, and `predict_score(features, items)`. The supplied code contains no backbone implementation, so the computation of sequence features and final user representation cannot be verified. Margin diagnosis uses features at aligned sequence positions; it does not explicitly select a final representation. Any final readout must respect left padding by selecting the final nonpadding position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the actual module as `view.model`, plus training histories and metadata references. The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape B × L. Sequences produce features through `log2feats`; stacked positive/negative IDs have shape B × L × 2 and are scored through `predict_score`.

`run_full_diagnosis` temporarily switches the model to evaluation mode, runs probes without gradients, and restores its previous mode.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 real item embeddings, excluding padding. It normalizes vectors, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result to [0, 1]. Around 0.5 means zero average cosine; near 1 indicates directional alignment. Lower values alone do not establish useful representations.
- **Positive–negative separation:** Processes at most ten loader batches. Positions qualify only when sequence, positive, and negative IDs are nonzero. It reports mean margin, 10th-percentile margin, fraction with negative margins, and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and smaller error/weak-separation rates generally indicate better training-pair discrimination.

Nonfinite embeddings or measured margins raise errors.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, ablation, or sensitivity perturbations run. Embedding subsampling uses seed 42; margin measurements use negatives supplied by the loader.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Metrics include `embedding_collapse_score`, four `pos_neg_*` margin statistics, and `pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`, which records valid-position/error counts and threshold. Category metadata availability is false; category lists are null. Insufficient embedding pairs or absent valid margins yield null measurements.

`diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds these measurements and definitions into a prompt requesting JSON status, findings, implications, and evidence. It does not itself generate that interpretation.

The probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, recommendation diversity, temporal sensitivity, or unobserved simulator traits.

Derivation: for n eligible positions indexed oldest-to-newest, retain the last K; position t is included with probability p_t=P(K≥n−t+1). If K is uniform on {1,…,n}, p_t=t/n. Thus per-batch normalization changes relative position/user contributions, beyond simply reducing training data. This follows from the random-denominator issue underlying self-normalized estimators ([Swaminathan and Joachims](https://www.cs.cornell.edu/People/tj/publications/swaminathan_joachims_15d.pdf)).

Direct recurrent precedents exist. [Tan et al. (2016)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.08117) train GRUs on every session prefix, each labeled with its immediately following item, and apply embedding dropout to generate pruned training inputs. Prefix expansion changes the supervised examples; it differs from removing an old prefix while retaining the same endpoint and next-item target. Standard [GRU4Rec](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) already supervises successive next-item transitions. CL4SRec is contrastive, not a Cloze masked-item reconstruction method. [Recency dropout](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11016) is another recurrent precedent, designed to counter excessive dependence on recent interactions; its motivation differs from discarding old context.
